text: Ten fictional nonprofit programme passages, each with two variants of three kinds: changed quantity, reordered and moved negation.

passages.source_passage: Since 2019, the Asha Bridge Health Collective has supported outreach clinics across 14 villages in the Sundarpur block of Kheral district. Baseline surveys found that only 38% of women attended four antenatal visits during their last pregnancy. Many mothers live more than two hours' walk from the nearest health post, and the block hospital offers emergency caesarean services during the day but not at night. Traditional birth attendants still assist roughly half of home deliveries, yet few have received refresher training. Families reported that transport costs, not distance alone, were the main reason they delayed seeking care. The proposed project will add three mobile teams, train 60 community midwives, and link each village to a referral ambulance by the end of 2026.

variants.changed_quantity_2: The proposed project will add three mobile teams, train 80 community midwives, and link each village to a referral ambulance

passages.source_passage: During the 2023 reporting year, the Mwangaza Savings Initiative supported 112 village savings and loan associations across the Tembe and Lusoni wards. Members saved a combined total of 41,600 dollars, an increase of 27% on the previous year. Women made up nine in ten members, and most groups elected a woman as chairperson and a man as treasurer. Repayment problems were reported not in Tembe but in Lusoni, where two groups delayed their share-out after a poor maize harvest. Members told field officers that in the first quarter they borrowed not for business stock but for school fees. No group reported losing its cash box to theft, which we attribute to the three-key system introduced in March. We intend to graduate 40 mature groups to independent status next year.

passages.source_passage: This update covers the third quarter of 2024 for the Kibali Community Health Trust programme in Nyarongo District. Our 248 community health workers completed 9,310 household visits, slightly above the quarterly target. Malaria testing kits ran short in September, so workers referred children with fever to the health centre instead of the dispensary. Stipends were paid on time in July and August but not in September, because the district transfer arrived late. Supervisors observed that refresher training improved not visit numbers but referral quality. Attrition stayed low: only six workers left, and none cited safety concerns. The board is asked to approve a 15% stipend increase so that pay keeps pace with local transport costs.

passages.source_passage: Session 3 of this guide prepares volunteers to lead hygiene meetings at the 22 boreholes built by the Kalunda Water Partnership in Mbelo Hills. Each meeting should last about 45 minutes and include a handwashing demonstration with soap and running water. Remind households that a latrine must be at least 30 metres from the borehole, never closer. Remember that tariff collection is the role not of the volunteer but of the water committee. When a pump breaks, report it to the committee first and the district office second. Children may attend the sessions but should not operate the pump handle alone. In our 2022 pilot, women attended more often in the mornings and men in the evenings, so plan two sessions where possible.

passages.source_passage: Since the last board meeting, the Velani Coast Early Warning Programme has installed sirens in 18 of its 25 target fishing villages. During the cyclone drill on 12 May, 71% of registered households reached an evacuation shelter within the 30-minute window. Messages were sent by SMS first and by loudspeaker second, which reached younger residents faster than older ones. Two shelters in Marisol have backup power for lighting but not for water pumps, and the district has not yet funded upgrades. The monthly radio checks are now run not by paid staff but by village volunteers. The flood gauge at the Tarra river mouth failed in April, so the district office relayed readings from the harbour master. We ask the board to release reserve funds for shelter upgrades before the monsoon.

passages.source_passage: In the six months to June 2024, the Haven Threads Family Service placed 37 children with approved foster carers in Kerrow Province. Family tracing teams located relatives for 19 children, and 11 of those reunifications have now been completed. Every placement was reviewed within 72 hours, although caseworkers visited rural homes less often than urban ones. No child was returned to a family before a home assessment had been signed off. Siblings were placed together in most cases, but not when the foster household lacked space. Two carers withdrew from the register, citing delayed allowances rather than child behaviour. The board should note that tracing across the northern border remains slow because the partner agency shares records on paper but not electronically.

passages.source_passage: This mid-term evaluation reviewed the first 18 months of the Sorvane Plateau cash transfer programme run by the Hearthline Relief Alliance. Enrolled households received 35 dollars per month through mobile money, and 4,200 households had been reached by March 2025. The share of households eating two or more meals a day rose from 52% to 74%. Transfers were spent mainly on food and only secondarily on livestock, contrary to early concerns. Evaluators found no evidence that transfers raised local market prices. However, payments arrived late in the lean season but not after the harvest, reducing their value when needs were highest. Recipients were consulted on the transfer amount but not on the payment schedule, a gap the second phase should address.

passages.source_passage: The Brightforge Skills Centre in Lorimba enrolled 320 young people in its first two intakes, against a target of 300. Courses in tailoring, solar installation and motorcycle repair ran for six months each. Six months after graduation, 58% of graduates were earning an income, mostly through self-employment rather than wage jobs. Young women chose tailoring more often than solar installation, and few enrolled in motorcycle repair. The apprenticeship component did not start on schedule, because only nine employers signed placement agreements in 2023. Graduates valued the practical workshops but not the classroom sessions on business planning. Evaluators recommend that start-up toolkits be given not three months later but at graduation, since many trainees could not begin working without them.

passages.source_passage: Tamsin Ridge camp hosts approximately 46,000 refugees, of whom an estimated 54% are children. Harbourlight Protection Partners has provided case management in the camp since 2021, handling 1,870 protection cases last year. Caseworkers currently refer survivors of violence to the medical post before the legal aid desk, which can delay documentation. There is no dedicated safe space for adolescent girls, and the existing women's centre closes at four in the afternoon. Unaccompanied children are registered on arrival but not assigned a caseworker until the following week. Language is a further barrier: Kiruvan, spoken by most new arrivals, is spoken by only three caseworkers, while most staff speak Dessic. Funding from this grant would not replace existing staff but would add a night-time response team.

passages.source_passage: In the 2023–24 school year, the Kanfa School Meals Partnership served daily hot lunches in 64 primary schools across Dorobe Region. On average, 18,500 pupils ate a meal on each school day, and enrolment rose by 9% compared with the previous year. Meals combined locally grown millet with fortified oil, and cowpeas were added twice a week. Deliveries reached schools on time in the dry months but not during the rains, when several roads flooded. Head teachers reported that attendance improved most among girls in the upper grades rather than among boys. Parent committees supplied firewood and cooks, while district staff handled storage audits. No school reported a food safety incident. Local sourcing targets were met for vegetables but not for grain, of which only 31% came from nearby farmers.
